criteria.rationale: Examined the 500-commit threshold, reliance on Git trace2 Bloom statistics, Git configuration semantics and sealed test evidence. The threshold is D1's explicit design choice; trace2 stability is a documented technical risk. Real Git 2.56 confirms the probe mechanism. Unsupported configuration behavior is separately reported as F24; fresh package execution was unavailable under the read-only boundary.

The feature adds synchronous CLI subprocess calls rather than shared concurrent runtime state. Each trace uses a unique temporary file with deferred removal; tests restore their threshold override and do not run these fixtures in parallel.

D1 puts repository maintenance behind doctor advice and explicit repair, addressing repeated expensive path-history lookups without mutating governance reads. Asking Git which filters it actually consults avoids duplicating alternate-object and graph-format selection logic. The three structural deltas expand permanent regression coverage for that behavior.

findings.action: commitGraphReadsDisabledBy treats every nonzero changedPathsVersion as usable. Read-only reproduction on Git 2.56 with commitGraph.changedPathsVersion=3: git config --type=int --get returns 3 successfully, while git log -1 --format=%H -- AGENTS.md exits zero and emits Bloom statistics with filter_not_present=1583, maybe=0 and definitely_not=0. Lines 167-172 return no configuration diagnosis, so doctor.go recommends a fixable rewrite. The installed git-config manual supports only -1, 0, 1 and 2; the Git binary also contains the diagnostic rejecting writes of unsupported versions. The advertised repair preserves this setting. Under R3, report a bounded actionable warning naming the unsupported configuration instead of recommending a rewrite, and add regression coverage.
